spots.name: Monument to Salavat Yulaev
spots.summary: The Monument to Salavat Yulaev is a monument to the Bashkir national hero Salawat Yulayev. It is located in Ufa, the capital city of the Republic of Bashkortostan in European Russia. The monument is represented in the coat of arms of Bashkortostan. It was built in 1967.

spots.summary: The Cathedral of the Nativity of the Theotokos is the largest Orthodox church in Ufa, Bashkortostan. It has been the seat of the Bishops of Ufa since May 2016.

spots.name: The Russian-Bashkir Friendship Monument
spots.summary: The Russian-Bashkir Friendship Monument is a monument in the city of Ufa, dedicated to the 400th anniversary of the accession of Bashkortostan in Russia, located on a hill above the Belaya River.

spots.name: Lenin Garden
spots.summary: Lenin Gardens was one of the first urban public parks in Ufa, Russia.

spots.summary: The main museum of the republic is located in the former building of the Peasant Land Bank (1905), which is interesting as the best Art Nouveau monument in Ufa. Ufa Muslim Cemetery
spots.summary: One of the oldest city cemeteries is located behind the television center, at the highest point of the Ufa Slope. It was supposedly established in the second half of the 19th century. Historic, pre-revolutionary graves have survived to the present day. spots.name: Aksakov Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri

spots.summary: The Memorial Aksakov Museum in Ufa is a writer's house biographical museum which commemorates the life and work of author Sergey Aksakov in an apartment where he lived in Ufa, Bashkortostan, Russia. It is located about two blocks from Republic House.

spots.name: Gostiny Dvor, Ufa
spots.summary: One of the largest shopping centres in Ufa is also an architectural monument. It was built in the first half of the 19th century on the main market square. This square was surrounded by merchant mansions, some of which have survived to modern times, albeit converted into something like a McDonald's: for example, three two-story buildings with corner towers from Lenin Street. spots.name: Lenin on Lenin St., Ufa
spots.summary: The first monument to Lenin in Ufa was erected in the autumn of 1924. Like all early monuments to Lenin, the project emphasized global socialist revolution. Lenin stood against the backdrop of a marble slab, crowned by a globe entangled in chains of imperialism (Nizhny Tagil has a similar monument, with Lenin standing on a globe). spots.name: Salavat Yulayev Garden, Ufa
spots.summary: This city garden was built here in 1900. Over the course of the 20th century, it went through four name changes, ultimately landing on Salavat Yulayev, the Bashkir national hero, a warrior-poet who participated in Pugachev's Rebellion. spots.summary: Opened in 1910 for German immigrants from the Baltic states, but from the 1930s until 2000 the Soviets used it as a warehouse. In 2016, an organ was added.

spots.name: Governor's House, Ufa
spots.summary: The Governor's House is an historic neoclassical building on the corner of Tukayeva Street and Sovetskaya Street, Ufa, the capital city of Bashkortostan, Russia. From the 1860s to the October Revolution of 1917, the house was the residence of the local governor.

spots.name: kilometer zero marker for the Bashkortostan Republic highway
spots.summary: This massive corner building with a seven-story tower was built in 1935-1936, and it's one of the best examples of Soviet architecture in Ufa. The first elevator in the city was unveiled here. spots.name: Majit Gafuri Memorial House
spots.summary: Писавший на татарском Мажит Гафури (1880-1934) считается, тем не менее, первым крупным башкирским поэтом. Деревянный дом на улице Гоголя был подарен Гафури в 1923 году. Внутри полностью реконструирована прижизненная обстановка, также неплохая экспозиция, рассказывающая о жизни и творчестве поэта. Сам дом со скромной, но очень стильной резьбой является одним из лучших образцов деревянной застройки

spots.name: Monument to Alexander Matrosov
spots.summary: The Monument to Alexander Matrosov is a monument in Ufa. It is located in close proximity to the Republic House.

spots.name: Kosterin's House
spots.summary: Kosterin's House is an historic Russian Art Nouveau former mansion on the corner of Pushkina and Karl Marx Streets, Ufa, Bashkortostan, Russia. Built in either 1907 or 1912 for merchant Pavel Kosterin, the building was occupied during the Russian Civil War by the White Army.

spots.name: Russian Academic Dramatic Theatre of Bashkortostan
Gentry Assembly Building, Ufa
spots.summary: This three-story, mid-19th century mansion is noteworthy because the great Russian opera singer, Fyodor Shalyapin, began his career here. Financially constrained, the young singer rented rooms in wooden houses on the outskirts - first in Trunilovskaya and then in the Bishop's settlement (none of these houses have been preserved). spots.name: Monument to Zagir Ismagilov
spots.summary: The Monument to Zagir Ismagilov is a monument to composer Zagir Ismagilov. It is located at Bashkir State Opera and Ballet Theatre in Ufa, Bashkortostan. It opened in 2008.

spots.name: Kommunisticheskaya 23 (Ufa)
spots.summary: The largest educational institution of pre-revolutionary Ufa was in this huge, three-story building on the corner of Kommunisticheskaya and Aksakova Streets. spots.name: Hudayberdin museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Shagit Hudayberdin was a Bashkir revolutionary active in the Russian Revolution. From 23 November 1921 to March 1922 he was the Responsible Secretary of the Bashkir Regional Committee of the All-Union Communist Party (Bolsheviks).

spots.name: Mayakovsky Square
spots.summary: A small, quiet, pleasant park at the intersection of Tsyurupy and Kommunistichesky streets. The square is filled with flowers, and there is also a monument to the great Soviet poet, Mayakovsky.
